name: Amrize Ltd
moat_justification: Cement and aggregates are local oligopolies by physics — transport costs wall off each market, permitted reserves are scarce and slow to replicate, and Amrize is North America's largest cement producer holding #1/#2 positions in 85% of its aggregates markets with ~46 years of aggregates and ~71 years of cement reserves. That earns real aggregates pricing power (+4.0% constant-currency in Q2 2026). Against: commodity products, equally scaled national rivals (CRH, Vulcan, Martin Marietta, Heidelberg), construction cyclicality, unproven standalone cement pricing (Q2 2026 cement price −0.2% constant-currency against oil-driven cost inflation that forced an EBITDA guidance cut), and structural energy/carbon costs. CAP = 9.8 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
THIN_HISTORY: only 3 fiscal years of data
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.2x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Strong NA building-materials franchise, moat 6/10, but at $37.32 the weighted IRR is 9.5% with IV@15% of $20.48 — clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$20.48.
moat_for: Largest cement producer in North America
#1/#2 position in 85% of aggregates markets served
Transport-cost local oligopolies in cement and aggregates
Scarce permitted reserves (~46 yrs aggregates, ~71 yrs cement)
Vertical integration: cement/aggregates to ready-mix to roofing
Demonstrated aggregates pricing power (+4.0% cc Q2 2026)
moat_against: Commodity products, no switching costs or brand protection
Equally scaled national rivals (CRH, Vulcan, Martin Marietta, Heidelberg)
Construction-cycle demand exposure; residential roofing soft
Cement pricing power unproven standalone (Q2 2026 price −0.2% cc vs cost inflation)
Energy and carbon-compliance cost headwinds on kilns
Growth capex step-up and bolt-on M&A consume moat cash flows
